name: SENSEI
notes: No live official SENSEI website was found: the INSPIRE record's listed homepage (http://home.fnal.gov/~javiert/sensei) returned HTTP 403 when requested on 2026-09-17 and again on 2026-10-25. links.website is left empty rather than guessed.

A ~100-gram SENSEI detector at SNOLAB was described as 'planned' in a 2020 SENSEI paper. The December 2023 SNOLAB paper (arXiv:2312.13342) reports a SENSEI detector there with six Skipper-CCDs of 2.19 g active mass each, installed in 2021 and run from 9 September 2022 to 10 April 2023; it does not report a ~100 g detector. The most recent SENSEI paper consulted (arXiv:2605.30281, May 2026) still places the operating detector 'near the MINOS cavern' at Fermilab, so no SNOLAB placement is recorded. A more recent, explicit SNOLAB-operations source would settle the SNOLAB status.

The detector is placed at the existing campus-level site (site:fermilab-main-campus), which is also used for the MINOS near detector hall (see that site's notes); no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives a more precise coordinate for the hall, so no separate hall site exists.

physics_goals.quote: we measure the lowest rates in silicon detectors of events containing one, two, three, or four electrons, and achieve world-leading sensitivity for a large range of sub-GeV dark matter masses
value: Detect sub-GeV dark matter via electron-recoil ionization signals in skipper-CCD silicon detectors

summary.plain: SENSEI uses ultra-sensitive silicon chips called skipper CCDs to hunt for very light dark matter particles, so light that they would only knock loose a handful of electrons. It has run in a shielded underground hall at Fermilab near Chicago since 2018.
summary.technical: Skipper-CCD dark matter search sensitive to electron recoils from sub-GeV dark matter, operating in the MINOS cavern at Fermilab; began with a ~0.1 g prototype device (2018-2019 shallow-underground run) and progressed to an improved ~2 g Skipper-CCD (2020 results), with operations continuing as of the May 2026 spurious-charge paper (arXiv:2605.30281). A ~100 g detector at SNOLAB was described as planned in 2020; the December 2023 paper (arXiv:2312.13342) reports a six-Skipper-CCD detector installed there in 2021 (2.19 g active mass per CCD), with a first science run from September 2022 to April 2023.

unique_capabilities.quote: We find zero events with three (or more) electrons in the unblinded data
value: Skipper-CCD readout allows sub-electron noise, enabling counting of individual ionization electrons (SENSEI's 2019 shallow-underground run found zero three-or-more-electron events in its unblinded data)
